[quote=the_commonwealth_provisional_states;61337904][b]Response to the Special Notice[/b]

From: Secretary of State, Alwin Rozen

To: My counterpart in the Dynastic Republic of Yzakastan

On behalf of the President of the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya. It is my greatest pleasure to inform you that your request to visit our nation's captial, District of Vespurya, Brookermeen has been accepted. We in Wuloosya value our storied partnership completely, and hope this state visit will increase our bilateral relations going into the 2030s and beyond. Accommodations for your visit will begin immediately 

The President of the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya accepts this personal gift from your government, and in return, gifts from our government will be prepared for President-Shah Orhan Izmýr should he decide to accept it.

(Gn)[/quote]

[b]January 27, 2028: The Vote Passes[/b]

Following several meetings with both the National Defense Committee, Senate Appropriations Committee, and various other interest groups, the Senate and Chamber would vote unanimously to permit the jumbo-jet to be given to the government of Wuloosya, though with one caveat: the government must purchase and give the jet utilizing the personal funds of the Shah.

With this matter secured, the formal trip plans began, with the Shah inviting Cahit Alparslan as a special guest on the trip.

A foreign communique would be sent to Wuloosya informing them that the Shah and Prelate of the Chamber of the Peoples would be arriving in the Wuloosyan capital by January 30, 2028.

[b]January 28, 2028: A meeting with the Femboy lobbyists[/b]

Cahit Alparslan did not wish to meet with a group that had seemingly popped out of thin air since the topic of Alaqar and its Femboy revolution had cropped up in Yzakastani sightlines; however, it was his unfortunate duty to meet with the group, for they had requested a meeting.

As Alparslan rolled into his office via a rear door, he noted a group of rather effeminate males seated on the couch; the suits they wore for professional purposes seemed too loose and baggy upon what Alparslan assumed was a male body. 

Greetings, gentlemen, began Cahit as an aide inserted and lit a cigar into Cahits mouth.

Greetings, replied one of the men, rising from the couch and approaching the desk of the prelate.

No, no, sit down, none of that, waved Cahit, blowing a puff of cigar smoke into the air, the folds of his cheeks jiggling slightly as he nodded his head, Now tell me what you want, so we can get this thing over with, he continued.

Well, sir, we seek to ask, humbly, that you consider supporting a vote for the bill to recognise the new regime of Alaqar, said one of the men in a higher-pitched voice than a man should have, at least according to Cahit.

Cahit knew that this was the case and waved his hand, a cloud of cigar smoke beginning to obscure him, Look, he said, Look here and look now, he continued, I am a good Yzak, I read the Quran, I attend the mosque, and am good friends with my local Mufti, he said, coughing slightly.

Of course, replied one of the men.

And of course, I am sure that you know that 47% of this country does about the same, along with another 34% who believe in Christ, said Cahit. 

Yes, Intoned another of the men.

Then why bother me with your pagan heathen antics? Asked Cahit, raising an eyebrow, which also seemed to raise one of his cheek folds like a curtain.

Because it is our right to ask that this state doesnt take military action against an innocent regime, replied one of the men hesitantly.

Look, I am going to be square with you, to use a Wuloosyan term, frankly Yzakastan has no interest in Alaqar or in their pagan femboy heathenism, we only care about stability, financial viability, and lowering our massive debt, which by the way is at 1.29 Trillion, if you havent seen, intoned Cahit.

Of course, and we thank you for your assurance, but wed want assurance from the Shah himself as well, replied the man.

The shah is busy, dammit, snarled Cahit, He doesnt have time for pansies and for degenerates, who the hell even allowed you here, intoned Cahit, looking around for an aide while tapping the panic button under his desk, Get the hell out! he roared, shaking and turning red, Coming here to test my patience, Ill have you beheaded! he jiggled as he attempted to lift himself from the wheel chair as two aides burst into the room to quickly usher out the terrified men who had begun to crowd towards the door.

Degenerates, pigs! Allah shall smite you! And your families! Youll be JAM! Turned into JAM! JAM to all of you! shouted Cahit, as an aide pulled a slipper out of the desk and threw it at the last man, striking him in the head. The man winced and ran out of the room.

It was clear that he was a man of stern composure, care, and of good manners. On the opposite side of him was the Prelate, a large, fat, bald old man, who had come in a motorised wheelchair, and seemed to have an affection for cigars, as he had chewn two since they had arrived.
